Toute rubrique sans source NASA lue = 'No NASA in-flight reference'.

regions.title: Head: attention, sleepiness, mood, sleep
regions.how: Daily keyboard check-in: sleepiness, stress, mood, workload, hours slept. Reaction time: run the 3-minute reaction-time test on the onboard tablet.
regions.how_src: C-Sync text: data/procedures/PROC-FATIGUE-01.json; method reference listed in SOURCES.md: Basner et al. 2011, PVT-B
regions.why: NASA's Human Research Program lists sleep-pattern disruptions and irregular light-dark cycles among spaceflight stressors that can affect health and mission success.
regions.when: Each value is compared with this astronaut's own first 5 days. One indicator away from baseline 2 days in a row → WATCH; two or more → DEGRADED. Two dimensions out of Normal → procedure PROC-FATIGUE-01 (IMPORTANT): crew medical officer.
regions.not: No clinical threshold. No label put on the person. No treatment or medication advice. The human decides.
regions.in_app: Coded: Attention (CO01, CO02) and Morale (PS01-PS04) in the drift rule; PH09 counts in Body.

regions.title: Chest: heart rate, reported symptom
indicators: SY01 Symptom reported by the crew member (body zone)
regions.how: Resting heart rate: wrist sensor, mean of 06:00-07:00. In a guided procedure: use the onboard device for heart rate and confirm the value shown on screen. Symptom: the crew member reports it and selects the body zone.
regions.why: NASA's Human Research Program reports that low gravity can alter the heart and blood vessels, and lists heart arrhythmias among the possible effects.
regions.when: Resting heart rate follows the drift rule (own baseline). A reported chest symptom opens PROC-EMERGENCY-01 at once (CRITICAL): guided measurements, report queued for the ground (flight surgeon), delivered once. To resume work, heart rate must be less than 10 minutes old.
regions.not: C-Sync does not interpret the symptom. No clinical threshold. No treatment or medication advice. Follow the onboard medical checklist and the crew medical officer.
regions.in_app: Coded: drift rule (PH01) and guided emergency (SY01). Zone selection in the app: not coded.

regions.title: Arm: blood pressure
indicators: PH10 Blood pressure (mmHg, SYS and DIA)
regions.how: Use the onboard device for blood pressure and confirm both values (SYS and DIA).
regions.why: NASA's Human Research Program lists low blood pressure, with a higher chance of fainting at landing, among the cardiovascular effects of spaceflight.
regions.when: No automatic alert: the values are recorded and added to the report for the crew medical officer and the ground.
regions.when_src: docs/OPEN_DECISIONS.md n°5 (default: shown only, M1 to confirm)
regions.not: No clinical threshold. No treatment or medication advice.
regions.in_app: Coded: recorded in the guided emergency; not part of the drift rule.

regions.title: Hand: blood glucose
indicators: PH12 Blood glucose (mg/dL), labelled 'no NASA in-flight reference'
regions.how: Use the onboard device for blood glucose and confirm the value shown on screen.
regions.when: No alert and no threshold: the value is recorded with the label 'no NASA in-flight reference'.
regions.not: No clinical threshold. No treatment or medication advice.
regions.in_app: Coded: recorded in the guided emergency only.

regions.title: Abdomen
regions.when: Shown as Unknown, never as Normal.
regions.when_src: csync/capsule.py (missing data never shown as normal)
regions.not: No estimate is made from other signals.

regions.title: Legs and bones
regions.when: Shown as Unknown, never as Normal.
regions.when_src: csync/capsule.py (missing data never shown as normal)
regions.not: No estimate is made from other signals.

regions.title: Whole body: temperature (immune system and personal radiation dose: not measured)
regions.how: Use the onboard device for body temperature and confirm the value shown on screen.
regions.when: Temperature: no automatic alert, recorded and added to the report. Items not measured are shown as Unknown, never as Normal.
regions.when_src: docs/OPEN_DECISIONS.md n°5 (default: shown only, M1 to confirm)
regions.not: No clinical threshold. No treatment or medication advice.
regions.in_app: Coded: temperature recorded in the guided emergency; not part of the drift rule.

regions.title: Habitat: ISS cabin (real NASA data)
regions.how: Automatic cabin sensors; no crew input. Data: NASA OSDR Environmental Data App, mission RR-1 (ISS, 2014).
regions.when: Context only, not evaluated: no state is triggered. Data-quality rule: a value frozen for 6 points or more is flagged as an artifact, never taken as normal. In the real RR-1 hourly CO2 series, one 37-hour run at 2646 ppm is flagged.
regions.not: No health conclusion is drawn from cabin data.
regions.in_app: Grey context card in the app; real telemetry used for data-quality checks.
regions.credit: Data and visualizations are courtesy of the Environmental Data App (EDA) (https://visualization.osdr.nasa.gov/eda/), Version # TODO_M1
